To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the distribution-based invariant neural networks, which we call Dida, are able to learn meta-features that characterize datasets.

Dida, an extension of deep learning architectures to learn invariant meta-features, achieves state-of-the-art results for two tasks at the dataset level, and that Dida can be trained with a small number of samples, which is a crucial property for meta-learning.
Dida, a novel architecture, is the first deep learning architecture to achieve invariances under permutation of both the input distribution samples and the features.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of deep neural networks that learn invariant representations of distributions of features.
distribution-based neural networks, invariant under permutation of features.
the development of a new architecture, Dida, which learns meta-features invariant under permutations of the samples and of the features, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Dida learns to represent the datasets in a meta-feature space, and that these meta-features are more powerful than those of the state of the arts, and are learned in a fully automatic way.

the proposed architecture Dida achieves a better performance than the state of the-art approaches in the tasks of predicting whether a dataset is a patch of another one, and of predicting whether the performance of a hyper-parameter configuration dominates that of another one.
Dida outperformed all the other methods on all the datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we proposed a new deep neural network architecture, called DIDA, which is robust to permutation of the input distribution and the features, and which outperforms the current state-of-the-art on the tasks of dataset patch similarity and hyperparameter configuration selection.
the Dida architecture can learn meta-features from distribution samples, invariant to the permutation of the samples and the features.

the proposed approach is the first to successfully combine deep learning from probability distribution with distribution-based meta-features, thus achieving state-of-the-art performances on two tasks of dataset characterization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Dida is able to extract a small number of meta-features that are able to characterize a dataset, and that are invariant under permutations of features and samples.
distribution-based architectures can be used as meta-features extractors, and that they are competitive with the state of the-art methods for meta-features extraction.
Dida, which is a simple architecture, achieves state-of-the-art results on two challenging meta-learning tasks.
